01.actor: A man who held a betrothal feast, and Rava
01.event: A man prepared a betrothal feast on the ninetieth day after a woman's first husband died, and Rava made him forfeit the feast.
01.turn: Rava prohibited the betrothal on that day; the Gemara then says it was really a marriage feast.
01.outcome: The feast was lost; the objection is answered by saying it was a marriage feast, not a betrothal feast.
01.summary: A man held a betrothal feast on the ninetieth day after the death of a woman's first husband. Rava ruled against it and the man lost his feast. The Gemara explains that the feast was in fact a marriage feast, which is forbidden, so the incident does not contradict the lenient view.
01.missing: Who the man was, how Rava intervened, and what happened to the feast; the incident is only alluded to as a challenge.

02.actor: A woman who owed an oath in Rav Beivai bar Abaye's court, and Rav Beivai
02.event: A woman obliged to take an oath asked for a document of her rights to be written for her before she swore; Rav Beivai ordered it written.
02.turn: The opposing litigant hoped she would be shamed into confessing in the town, but she demanded a document first and Rav Beivai agreed; Rav Pappi then rebuked him with a harsh play on his family's name.
02.outcome: Rav Beivai ordered the document written; Rav Pappi objected sharply.
02.summary: A woman was ordered to swear an oath in Rav Beivai bar Abaye's court. Her opponent suggested she swear in her town, where shame might make her confess. She asked that a document of her rights be written first, to be handed to her when she swore, and Rav Beivai told the judges to write it. Rav Pappi rebuked him, asking whether he spoke unfortunate words because he came from an unfortunate family.
02.missing: Whether the document was in the end written or the oath taken.

03.actor: Rabbi Yehuda, the Elders and the residents of Avel
03.event: Residents drew water on Shabbat from the channel running from Avel to Tzippori by authority of the Elders, without extra partitions.
03.turn: The Sages reply that this was no proof, since the channel was too small to need a partition.
03.summary: Rabbi Yehuda cited a precedent of a water channel from Avel to Tzippori from which people drew water on Shabbat on the Elders' authority. The Sages answered that it proved nothing, because the channel was shallower or narrower than the minimum size that needs a partition.
03.missing: It is a precedent cited in an argument, with no scene, characters or sequence beyond the report.

04.actor: A blind man who reviewed mishnayot before Mar Shmuel
04.event: The blind man was late; Mar Shmuel's messenger went after him by a different road and on returning said the man's wife had committed adultery.
04.turn: The blind man arrived by another route, the messenger missed him, then reported the accusation.
04.outcome: Mar Shmuel told him to divorce her if he trusted the messenger, and not to if he did not.
04.summary: A blind man who regularly reviewed mishnayot before Mar Shmuel did not show up one day. Shmuel sent a messenger to fetch him, but they took different roads and missed each other. The messenger came back and claimed that the blind man's wife had committed adultery. The blind man went to Shmuel, who told him to divorce her if he trusted the messenger, and not otherwise.

05.actor: The daughters-in-law of Abdan and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi
05.event: The daughters-in-law of Abdan rebelled against their husbands and Rabbi sent two Sages to examine them.
05.turn: Other women told them their husbands were coming and they answered 'Let them be your husbands'.
05.outcome: Rabbi said there is no greater refusal than this.
05.summary: The daughters-in-law of Abdan rebelled against their husbands, and Rabbi sent two Sages to examine the matter. When other women warned them that their husbands were coming, they replied, 'Let them be your husbands.' Rabbi declared that there is no greater refusal than that.

06.event: Rabbi Yoḥanan was expounding about burning notar when Rabbi Elazar objected from a baraita and silenced him.
06.turn: After Rabbi Elazar left, Rabbi Yoḥanan praised him as expounding like Moses from the Almighty, and Reish Lakish said it was only a baraita in Torat Kohanim.
06.outcome: Rabbi Yoḥanan went out, learned all of Torat Kohanim in three days and mastered it in three months.
06.summary: Rabbi Yoḥanan was teaching a law about burning notar when Rabbi Elazar raised a baraita against him that Yoḥanan could not answer, so he fell silent. After Elazar left, Yoḥanan praised him to Reish Lakish, who replied that the teaching was just a baraita from Torat Kohanim. Yoḥanan went off, learned the entire work in three days and mastered it in three months.

07.actor: The daughter-in-law of Nakdimon ben Guryon and the Sages
07.event: The Sages apportioned her two se'a of wine for pudding from one Shabbat eve to the next.
07.turn: She blessed them that they should apportion the same for their own daughters.
07.outcome: The Sages did not say amen, because she was a widow awaiting her yavam and they did not want that fate for their daughters.
07.summary: When Nakdimon ben Guryon's daughter-in-law was widowed, the Sages set aside two se'a of wine for her pudding each week. She said to them, 'So may you apportion for your own daughters.' The Sages did not answer amen, since she was a widow waiting for a yavam and they did not want their daughters to share her condition.

08.actor: A childless woman and Rabbi Ami
08.event: A woman came to Rabbi Ami demanding her marriage-contract payment and a divorce because her husband could not father children.
08.turn: Rabbi Ami first dismissed her as not commanded to procreate; she asked who would care for her in old age.
08.outcome: Rabbi Ami ruled that in such a case the husband is certainly forced to divorce her.
08.summary: A woman came before Rabbi Ami and demanded her marriage contract payment, wanting a divorce from a husband who could not father children. He told her to go away since she was not commanded to be fruitful and multiply. She asked what would become of her in old age, and he then said that in such a case the husband is certainly compelled to divorce her.

09.missing: It is a cryptic riddle-answer to a question about where Rabbi Elai is hiding; no event or turn occurs.

10.actor: A man who had never been married, and Rav Naḥman
10.event: The man came before Rav Naḥman claiming he had found an unobstructed orifice at consummation.
10.turn: Rav Naḥman inferred he must have had experience with prostitutes, since he had never been married.
10.outcome: Rav Naḥman ordered him flogged with palm branches.
10.summary: A man who had never been married came before Rav Naḥman and said he had found an open orifice on his wedding night. Rav Naḥman reacted by saying to flog him, since a bachelor could only know such a thing if prostitutes were common around him.

11.event: Ravin went as agent to betroth a woman for his son and betrothed her to himself.
11.turn: The Gemara objects that this is deceitful; the woman's family would give her only to the father, and he did not go back to inform his son for fear someone else would betroth her.
11.outcome: His conduct is justified on those grounds.
11.summary: Ravin the Pious was sent to betroth a woman to his son but ended up betrothing her to himself. The Gemara asks how a pious man could act so deceitfully, and answers that her family would not give her to the son. He did not return to tell his son because he feared someone else would betroth her in the meantime.

12.event: Passed over for head of the yeshiva, Ilfa hung himself from a ship's mast and swore to fall and drown unless he could derive any baraita brought to him from a mishna.
12.turn: An old man taught him a baraita from the Tosefta and asked where it appears in the Mishna.
12.outcome: Ilfa answered that it follows Rabbi Meir, who says it is a mitzva to fulfill the words of the dead, and so met the challenge.
12.summary: Ilfa suspended himself from a ship's mast and declared he would fall and drown if someone brought him a baraita from the school of Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rabbi Oshaya that he could not trace to a mishna. An old man came and taught him a baraita about a dying father's instructions for his sons' allowance. Ilfa asked whose opinion it was and answered that it was Rabbi Meir's, that one must fulfill the words of the dead, and thus passed the test.
12.missing: The first sentence of the background (the appointment of Rabbi Yoḥanan) appears only in editorial commentary inside [4].

13.event: Absorbed in study, Rav Reḥumi failed to come home on the eve of Yom Kippur as he did every year.
13.turn: His wife waited, grew distressed and shed a tear.
13.outcome: At that moment the roof he was sitting on collapsed and he died.
13.summary: Rav Reḥumi studied before Rava and used to come home every Yom Kippur eve. One year he was engrossed in study and did not come. His wife kept saying 'now he is coming', then grew upset and a tear fell. At that moment the roof he sat on collapsed and he died.

14.missing: It is a halakhic question about a slave who joined an army, a search for a source, a rebuttal and a ruling; there is no narrative event beyond the exchange of legal arguments.

15.actor: A maidservant of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's household and Rabbi
15.event: The maidservant immersed and came up with a bone found between her teeth.
15.turn: The bone was discovered after immersion.
15.outcome: Rabbi required her to immerse again.
15.summary: A maidservant in Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's household immersed herself and, on coming up, a bone was found between her teeth. Rabbi required her to immerse a second time.
15.missing: Cited as evidence in a legal argument; why it happened or any details are not given.

16.missing: It is a recollection of a repeated habit of Rabbi Yoḥanan eating fruit and swearing, used as a proof in a legal argument, not a single narrated event.

17.actor: The Sages of Babylonia, the witnesses, Abaye and Rava
17.event: A bill of divorce was found in Sura signed by Anan bar Ḥiyya of Neharde'a; the Sages searched and found only one other man of that name, Anan of Ḥagra, whom witnesses said was with them in Neharde'a that day.
17.turn: The witnesses' testimony conflicted with the place named in the document.
17.outcome: Abaye said he is not concerned about the other man; Rava said we are concerned because he might have travelled by miracle or given verbal instructions; no ruling is stated in these segments.
17.summary: A bill of divorce turned up in Sura, written in the name of Anan bar Ḥiyya of Neharde'a. The Sages searched and found only one other man with that name, Anan of Ḥagra, but witnesses said he had been with them in Neharde'a on that day. Abaye said there is no concern about him, while Rava said that concern is warranted since he might have got there by miracle or given verbal instructions.
17.missing: No clear resolution of what happened to the bill of divorce; the passage moves into legal argument.

18.actor: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
18.event: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba met Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi with a covering on his head hurrying his child to the synagogue and asked why the fuss.
18.turn: Rabbi Yehoshua answered that the verse about making things known to one's sons is juxtaposed to the day at Horeb.
18.outcome: From then on Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba would not eat before teaching a child, and Rabba bar Rav Huna would not eat before bringing a child to the study hall.
18.summary: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba found Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi rushing his child to the synagogue with an improvised head covering. Asked why, Rabbi Yehoshua said that teaching one's children is placed beside the revelation at Sinai. After this, Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba would not eat until he had taught a child, and Rabba bar Rav Huna would not eat until he had brought a child to the study hall.

19.missing: It is a legal argument about what Shmuel meant; the one mention of Shmuel telling Rav Ḥana to gather ten men is only a cited statement, not a narrated event.

20.actor: Rabbi Abba bar Shumni and Rav Menashya bar Yirmeya
20.event: Two scholars parting at the ford of the Yofti River agreed each would say something the other had not heard.
20.turn: One taught a definition of drinking versus intoxication; the other taught what one does with a convert's property.
20.outcome: The scene ends in a series of halakhic teachings with no further event.
20.summary: Two scholars, Rabbi Abba bar Shumni and Rav Menashya bar Yirmeya, were saying goodbye at a river crossing and agreed each would share a teaching the other had not heard. One defined the difference between a drunk and an intoxicated person by whether he can speak before a king. The other taught that someone who took a convert's property should buy a Torah scroll.
20.missing: The framing scene is brief and the rest is a list of rulings, so there is no real turn or ending.
